Stated Claim / Post Context:
Gun control nut spray paints 9/11 Memorial with ‘Just Stop Killing Kids’ in broad daylight stunt

A gun control nut vandalized the 9/11 Memorial Reflecting Pool with red spray paint in a broad daylight political stunt.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A gun control nut vandalized the 9/11 Memorial Reflecting Pool with red spray paint in a broad daylight political stunt.

Jonathan Andrew Tijerina, 31, was arrested and charged with criminal mischief and making graffiti for tagging a section of the North Tower reflecting pool with the name of his website Monday evening, police said, according to CBS News New York.

“Juststopkillingkids.com,” read the red spray-painted markings written across the names of dozens of victims engraved into the memorial at the footprint of the Sept. 11, 2001 terror attack.

Tijerina, 31, took credit for the vile desecration, posting video of himself in the midst of the act.

The alleged vandal recorded the entire stunt from start to finish, capturing himself walking up to the memorial, pulling a spray can out of his bag and writing his message across several panels, according to several videos posted to Instagram.

Tijerina identified himself as the person behind the vandalism that cost over $2,500 in damages, according to police.

“My name is Jon Tijerina and I’ve just spray-painted ‘just stop killing kids’ on the 9/11 Memorial,” Tijerina boasted.

The 9/11 Memorial and Museums announced it had removed the spray paint, returning the memorial to its previous state.

“The 9/11 Memorial is a sacred place of reflection at the heart of a rebuilt World Trade Center that honors the 2,983 victims killed in the September 11, 2001 and February 26, 1993 terrorist attacks. Yesterday’s brief incident was swiftly addressed by security staff and law enforcement, and the impacted area was immediately restored to its commemorative state,” a spokesperson told CBS New York.

Tijerina’s website promoted “nonviolent civil resistance” as the answer to his campaign, saying it was the way to change laws and society.

Tijerina promoted his arrest as a win, attempting to get the attention of President Trump and NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

“On October 26, 2026, Jon Tijerina was arrested for spraying red paint on Freedom Tower in NYC. He is demanding that Trump and Mamdani enforce common-sense, highly popular demands with respect to guns such as Universal Background Checks and a National Gun Registry,” Tijerina’s organization wrote in a follow-up post.

He cited the mass shooting after the Florida A&M homecoming football game as a reason for his alleged vandalism.

Tijerina’s “civil resistance organization” made two demands to “Just Stop Killing Kids” – calling for universal background checks and universal gun registry.

“We have two specific, achievable demands. Both have majority public support. Both already exist in other high-income countries. Neither requires repealing the Second Amendment. We are not asking for the impossible — we are asking for what every other wealthy democracy already has,” the website states.

Tijerina complained Monday that another one of his political protests, a recent seven-day fast didn’t receive any attention.

His alleged weeklong protest was to demand 2 million affordable housing units be made available in the city within 5 years.

Senate control is a coin flip — and Democrats’ path runs through Trump Country

With Election Day six days away, Fox News Power Rankings rate Senate control a toss-up as Democrats aim to flip seats in Trump country states.

Actual Article Body:

MAGA voters speaking with Fox News Digital outside a President Donald Trump headlined rally in Port Huron, Michigan defend the president amid rising prices and the Iran War: 'He's doing what he has to do.'

With six days to go until Election Day, the battle for control of the Senate appears to be a jump ball, with the road to the majority running mostly through states President Donald Trump won in 2024.

While the final Fox News Power Rankings ahead of the midterms revealed three key shifts in the direction of the Democrats, their hopes of retaking the Senate hinge on flipping seats in so-called Trump Country.

As they fight to hold their slim House and Senate majorities, Republicans are fighting political history, as the party in power in Washington has traditionally lost seats during midterm election years. The GOP also faces a challenging political climate fueled by persistent inflation tied in part to what polls show is an unpopular war with Iran and Trump's increasingly negative approval ratings.

FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS: AS IRAN LOOMS LARGE, CAN THE GOP KEEP THE FAITHFUL?

Fox News Power Rankings on Senate forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

Republicans currently control the Senate 53-47, with the Fox News Power Rankings rating the race for Senate control a toss-up.

Both parties are three seats short of a majority, according to the forecast. Democrats are favored in 48 seats and Republicans are ahead in 47. The GOP needs to hold 50 seats to retain control of the chamber, since Republican Vice President JD Vance is the tie-breaking vote in the Senate.

If Democrats ride a blue wave to victory by winning most or all of the competitive races, they could potentially come away from the midterms with up to 53 seats.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Fox News Power Rankings on Senate forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

But if Republicans have a good night and defy expectations, the GOP could hold the majority with up to 52 seats, according to the forecast.

Ohio is one of the three shifts Fox News made in the final Power Rankings. It shifted from toss-up to Lean Democrat. Meanwhile, South Carolina moved from Likely Republican to Lean Republican, and Mississippi from Solid Republican to Likely Republican.

DEMOCRACY 2026: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Fox News Power Rankings on Senate forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

In red-leaning Ohio, former longtime Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown is challenging appointed GOP Sen. Jon Husted in the race to fill the final two years of the Senate term that then-Sen. Vance won in 2022.

In solidly Republican South Carolina, Democratic challenger Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, is taking on appointed Sen. Darlene Graham in the race to succeed the senator's older brother, the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, who unexpectedly died in July.

And in Mississippi, a state Trump carried by 33 points two years ago, Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith faces a challenge from Democratic District Attorney Scott Colom.

Kansas, another red state, remains Lean Republican in the final Power Rankings. GOP Sen. Roger Marshall is facing a rough re-election as he battles Democrat Adam Hamilton, a pastor.

CHECK OUT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POLLS IN THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS

Fox News Power Rankings on Senate forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

Republicans are also playing defense in Alaska, Iowa, Maine and Texas, which are all rated toss-ups in the Power Rankings.

In red-leaning Alaska, GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan faces former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola. In Republican-controlled Iowa, GOP Rep. Ashley Hinson and Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek are battling to succeed retiring Republican Sen. Joni Ernst.

Longtime Republican Sen. Susan Collins is fighting for re-election in blue-leaning Maine against Democratic challenger Troy Jackson, a former state Senate president. And in red-leaning Texas, state Attorney General Ken Paxton is locked in an expensive and contentious showdown with Democratic state Rep. James Talarico in the race to succeed longtime GOP Sen. John Cornyn, who was ousted by Paxton in a combustible Republican primary.

Republicans hope to go on offense in Michigan, the fifth state listed as a toss-up in the Power Rankings. Former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers is taking on Abdul El-Sayed, the Democrats' nominee, in the race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.

Fox News Power Rankings on Senate forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

The GOP is also trying to flip Senate seats in two blue states listed as Lean Democrat.

In New Hampshire, former Republican Sen. John E. Sununu is facing off against Rep. Chris Pappas, a Democrat, in the race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen.

Meanwhile, in blue-tilting Minnesota where Democratic Sen. Tina Smith is retiring, Republican nominee Michele Tafoya, a former longtime NBC sportscaster, is taking on Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, a Democrat.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

With less than a week until Election Day, there are still plenty of undecided votes.

"In Alaska, Iowa and Kansas, three states with recent high-quality polling, an average of 10% of voters say they haven’t decided who they will support or won’t support the major candidates," noted Remy Numa, a Fox News contributor who steers the network's Power Rankings.
